items.title:
Anthropic has filed for an IPO, with its prospectus revealing just how fast the company is scaling.
FY25 revenue jumped 1,088% YoY to $4.59B, while compute and infrastructure spending rose 190% to $7.33B.
The company posted an $8.06B operating loss and ended 2025 with $20.28B in cash and short-term investments.
Anthropic’s two largest direct customers accounted for 24% of total revenue combined.
items.title_ja:
Anthropic は IPO を申請しており、その目論見書により同社がいかに急速に拡大しているかが明らかになりました。
25 年度の収益は前年比 1,088% 増の 45 億 9000 万ドルとなり、コンピューティングとインフラストラクチャへの支出は 190% 増の 73 億 3000 万ドルとなりました。
同社は80億6000万ドルの営業損失を計上し、2025年終了時点では202億8000万ドルの現金と短期投資を残した。
Anthropic の 2 つの最大の直接顧客は、合計収益の 24% を占めました。

items.title:
Chinese AI and lab-robotics company MegaRobo has raised nearly $200 million from investors including Oman's sovereign wealth fund, the Oman Investment Authority, per Bloomberg.
CMB International also joined, along with existing backers Asia Investment Capital, Granite Asia and Sinovation Ventures. MegaRobo did not disclose its valuation.
Its last big raise was a $300 million Series C in 2022, led by GGV Capital, Asia Investment Capital and Goldman Sachs.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグによると、中国のAIおよび実験用ロボット企業メガロボは、オマーンの政府系ファンドであるオマーン投資庁を含む投資家から2億ドル近くを調達した。
CMB International も、既存の支援者である Asia Investment Capital、Granite Asia、Sinovation Ventures とともに参加しました。メガロボは評価額を明らかにしていない。
最後の大規模調達は、GGVキャピタル、アジア・インベストメント・キャピタル、ゴールドマン・サックス主導による2022年のシリーズCで3億ドルだった。

items.title:
Anthropic raised about $81 billion in its upsized IPO, selling roughly 980 million shares at $83, up from the 825 million it first planned, per Reuters.
Reuters calls it the biggest IPO ever. It tops the $75 billion SpaceX raised in June, though SpaceX reached $85.7 billion after its underwriters bought extra shares.
Anthropic itself sold about 956 million of the shares; existing holders sold the rest.
items.title_ja:
ロイター通信によると、アンスロピックは大規模なIPOで約810億ドルを調達し、当初計画していた8億2,500万株を83ドルで約9億8,000万株から売却した。
ロイターはこれを史上最大のIPOと呼んでいる。これはスペースXが6月に調達した750億ドルを上回っているが、引受会社が追加株を買い取ったことでスペースXは857億ドルに達した。
アンスロピック自体は約9億5,600万株を売却した。既存のホルダーが残りを売却しました。

items.title:
Anthropic's $83 IPO price values it at about $1.49 trillion fully diluted, per the FT.
It scaled up the deal late Wednesday after a glut of demand. With a $26 billion private placement from Nvidia, Microsoft and Google, it will have over $200 billion on its balance sheet.
items.title_ja:
FTによると、アンスロピックの83ドルのIPO価格は完全希薄化後の価値として約1兆4900億ドルに相当する。
過剰な需要を受けて水曜日遅くに取引を拡大した。 Nvidia、Microsoft、Googleからの260億ドルの私募により、同社の貸借対照表には2000億ドル以上が残ることになる。

items.title:
Palo Alto Networks is buying AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion, per the WSJ.
The startup was founded last year by three former OpenAI researchers. It was valued at $3.25 billion in a funding round announced earlier this month.
items.title_ja:
WSJによると、パロアルトネットワークスはAIスタートアップのアプライド・コンピューティングを45億ドルで買収するとのこと。
このスタートアップは昨年、OpenAI の元研究者 3 人によって設立されました。今月初めに発表された資金調達ラウンドでは32億5000万ドルと評価された。

items.title:
Anthropic has priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its $70-$78 range, per Bloomberg.
At $83, the 825 million shares in its filing would raise about $68.5 billion. SpaceX's record IPO raised $75 billion in June.
Trading starts Thursday on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグによると、アンスロピックはIPOの価格を1株あたり83ドルと、70～78ドルの範囲を上回っている。
83ドルで、申請書類にある8億2,500万株は約685億ドルを調達することになる。スペースXは6月に記録的なIPOで750億ドルを調達した。
ナスダックではティッカーANTで木曜日に取引が開始される。

items.title:
Anthropic is weighing pricing its IPO at up to $85 a share, above its $70-$78 range, per Bloomberg.
At $85, the 825 million shares on offer would raise about $70 billion, or $81 billion with the extra allotment. That would still fall short of SpaceX's record $85.7 billion.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグによると、アンスロピックはIPOの価格を1株あたり70～78ドルの範囲を上回る最大85ドルにすることを検討しているという。
85ドルで売り出される8億2,500万株は約700億ドル、追加割り当てを含めると810億ドルを調達することになる。それでもスペースXの過去最高額である857億ドルには及ばない。

items.title:
Bret Taylor's AI agent startup Sierra is in talks to raise money at a $30 billion valuation, per The Information.
That's nearly double the $15.8 billion it was valued at in May, and triple its $10 billion valuation in September 2025.
items.title_ja:
The Information によると、ブレット・テイラー氏の AI エージェントのスタートアップである Sierra は、評価額 300 億ドルで資金調達に向けて交渉中だという。
これは5月時点の評価額158億ドルのほぼ2倍で、2025年9月時点の評価額100億ドルの3倍となっている。

items.title:
Lyme disease vaccine developer VitriVax raised $87 million in a Series C from investors including F-Prime, NEA, Eli Lilly and Sanofi Ventures.
There's no approved Lyme vaccine for people today. The only one that ever reached the market, LYMErix, was pulled in 2002.
items.title_ja:
ライム病ワクチン開発者のVitriVaxは、F-Prime、NEA、Eli Lilly、Sanofi Venturesなどの投資家からシリーズCで8,700万ドルを調達した。
現在、人々に使用できる承認されたライムワクチンはありません。これまでに市場に出回った唯一の LYMErix は 2002 年に廃止されました。

items.title:
Coal India's Mahanadi Coalfields raised more than $245 million from anchor investors, including Abu Dhabi's ADIA and India's LIC, ahead of its IPO, per Reuters.
The IPO opens Thursday at ₹129-136 a share, valuing the coal miner at up to about $9.6 billion.
items.title_ja:
ロイター通信によると、コール・インディアのマハナディ・コールフィールドズは、IPOに先立ち、アブダビのADIAやインドのLICなどの主要投資家から2億4500万ドル以上を調達した。
IPOは木曜日に1株当たり129〜136ルピーで開始され、炭鉱会社の評価額は最大約96億ドルとなる。

items.title:
Endpoint security company IGEL is now valued at more than $1 billion after a strategic investment from Vitruvian Partners.
Vitruvian joins backer TA Associates. IGEL's locked-down operating system helps companies restore access to Windows PCs hit by ransomware or outages.
items.title_ja:
エンドポイント セキュリティ会社 IGEL は、Vitruvian Partners からの戦略的投資を受けて、現在 10 億ドル以上の評価を受けています。
Vitruvian が後援者の TA Associates に加わりました。 IGEL のロックダウンされたオペレーティング システムは、企業がランサムウェアや機能停止の被害を受けた Windows PC へのアクセスを復元するのに役立ちます。

items.title:
New York City's comptroller says he is "not done fighting yet" as Anthropic pushes ahead with its IPO this week, per Bloomberg.
Mark Levine, who oversees more than $325 billion in city pension money, asked Anthropic in October to pause the listing over AI safety concerns.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグによると、アンスロピックが今週IPOを進める中、ニューヨーク市の会計監査官は「まだ戦いは終わっていない」と述べた。
3,250億ドル以上の市年金を管理しているマーク・レバイン氏は10月、AIの安全性への懸念を理由にアンスロピックに対し、上場を一時停止するよう要請した。

items.title:
Longevity startup Hone Health raised $228 million in a round led by Jay-Z's MarcyPen Capital Partners, with Gwyneth Paltrow's Kinship Ventures and the Jonas Brothers also investing.
Only $28 million is equity. The other $200 million is growth financing from General Catalyst.
items.title_ja:
長寿スタートアップのホーン・ヘルスは、ジェイ・Zのマーシーペン・キャピタル・パートナーズ主導のラウンドで2億2800万ドルを調達し、グウィネス・パルトロウのキンシップ・ベンチャーズとジョナス・ブラザーズも投資した。
資本はわずか 2,800 万ドルです。残りの 2 億ドルは General Catalyst からの成長資金です。

items.title:
Anthropic's IPO has drawn nearly $500 billion in orders, about $400 billion from institutions and close to $100 billion from retail, CNBC reports. The orders are nonbinding.
Anthropic is considering selling more shares and pricing well above $80, above its $70 to $78 range.
items.title_ja:
CNBCの報道によると、アンスロピックのIPOでは5,000億ドル近くの注文が集まり、そのうち機関投資家からは約4,000億ドル、小売店からは1,000億ドル近くの注文があったという。命令には拘束力はありません。
アンスロピックはさらに株を売却し、70～78ドルの範囲を上回る80ドルを大きく超える価格設定を検討している。

想定仮条件は2,340〜2,590円で、平均の2,465円で計算すると時価総額は約3,813億円。
2026年のIPOでは時価総額、調達規模ともに最大の案件です。
新株の発行はなく、既存株主による売り出しのみです。売出株数はオーバーアロットメントを含めると約4,915万株、約1,211億円になります。
グローバル・オファリングで、主幹事は野村證券、SMBC日興証券、BofA証券、ゴールドマン・サックス証券です。
前身のワークスアプリケーションズが次世代製品「HUE」の開発失敗と顧客との訴訟で経営難に陥り、2019年8月に会社分割で切り出したHR事業をベインキャピタルが取得しました。取得額は約1,000億円とみられています。
2023年7月、ベインは新ファンドから再出資し、シンガポール政府系ファンドのGICとの共同保有に移行しました。
その後、2024年にサイダスを約66億円、2025年にエンバーポイントを約228億円で取得しました。エンバーポイントはベイン傘下からの取得です。現在の保有比率は、完全希薄化ベースでベイン56.78%、GIC39.88%です。
2025年12月期は、売上収益657億円（前期比21.9%増）、調整後EBITDAは305億円（同27.2%増）で、マージンは46%でした。2026年1〜9月期は、売上収益562億円（同18.0%増）、調整後EBITDA291億円（同23.0%増）で、マージンは52%まで上がっています。
一方、最終損益は1〜9月期で赤字です。借り換えに伴う手数料の一括費用化や、合併で税務上の繰越欠損金を一部引き継げなかったことが響きました。
顧客基盤の強さは際立っています。
・導入先：約1,200法人グループ
・年間解約率：1.0%
・NRR：112%
・契約10年以上の顧客：66%
・クラウド比率：2021年末の16.8%から2026年9月末に81.5%
大企業の給与計算は一度入れると替えにくく、クラウド移行による単価アップを着実に取り込んでいます。
2023年の再出資時の株主資本は約1,547億円、1株1,000円です。想定価格2,465円なら株式ベースで約2.5倍、約3.4年のIRRで30%前後と試算できます。
純有利子負債は約1,750億円で、時価総額に足した企業価値は約5,560億円で、直近12カ月の調整後EBITDA約359億円に対するEV/EBITDAは約15.5倍です。10月に報じられた「企業価値ベースで5,000億円超」になっています
ただし、今回売却するのは保有株の3割程度にとどまり、上場後もファンドが約3分の2を保有し続ける計算です。
リターンの大半は上場後の株価次第で、残りを段階的に売っていく形になります。
2019年取得分のベイン旧ファンドは、企業価値ベースで約1,000億円から約3,500億円へ約3.5倍にしていて、レバレッジを考えると、株式ベースのリターンはそれ以上です。

Anthropic has officially priced its IPO at $83 per share, above its original expected range of $70–$78, with trading expected to begin on the Nasdaq tomorrow.
This is one of the largest IPOs in stock market history and a major moment for the AI industry. The company increased its offering from 825 million shares to 980 million shares, bringing the total offering to approximately $81.3 billion. Of that, Anthropic itself will receive roughly $79.4 billion before fees, while existing shareholders will receive approximately $2 billion. This gives Anthropic an enormous amount of additional capital to invest in computing infrastructure, model training, and expanding its operations. What's particularly interesting is the valuation. At $83 per share, Anthropic is reportedly valued at approximately $1.08 trillion on a basic share count basis and around $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis. Revenue growth has been extraordinary, reaching $33.2 billion in the first nine months of 2026, compared with $4.6 billion for all of 2025. However, the company is still operating at a loss and faces enormous computing costs.
I think the timing is especially interesting considering all the concerns surrounding AI spending, valuations, and the sustainability of the AI trade. Yet Anthropic has managed to price above its original range while increasing the number of shares offered, suggesting institutional demand remains incredibly strong. That said, a successful IPO doesn't necessarily make it a great investment at any price. Competition from OpenAI, Google, and other frontier labs remains intense, and investors are already pricing in years of extraordinary growth. I'll be watching where the stock actually opens tomorrow because retail investors aren't guaranteed the $83 IPO price, and a significant opening premium could make an already expensive valuation even harder to justify.

Hedge funds are selling tech stocks like the AI trade is officially over.
According to Goldman Sachs, hedge funds are selling technology stocks at a pace we haven't seen in nearly a decade. Their long to short ratio in tech has also fallen to its lowest level since 2016, which tells you just how aggressively institutions are reducing their exposure. And I think a lot of this has to do with how crowded the AI trade became over the past couple of years. Many of these funds made enormous amounts of money investing in AI companies, but now they're worried about protecting those gains as concerns around valuations, AI spending, and the sustainability of the entire AI infrastructure buildout continue growing. And to be fair, I can understand some of those concerns. We're talking about hundreds of billions of dollars being invested into AI infrastructure, and investors are increasingly questioning when these companies will start seeing meaningful returns on that spending.
But here's what I find interesting. A lot of these companies are still reporting incredible revenue growth, demand for AI infrastructure remains strong, and their underlying businesses haven't necessarily deteriorated nearly as much as their stock prices would suggest. I think we're seeing a combination of legitimate concerns and hedge funds simply wanting to get out of the way before things potentially get worse. And here's the other side of this. When institutions have already sold this aggressively, you have to wonder how much selling pressure is actually left. If earnings continue holding up and sentiment improves, these same funds could eventually have to come back and buy the stocks they just sold. Now, I'm not saying we've reached the bottom, because things could absolutely get worse from here. But I do think we're getting to a point where sentiment is becoming increasingly disconnected from the long term potential of some of these companies. Personally, I'm still bullish on AI over the long term. I just think the market is going through a pretty significant reset right now, and for patient investors, that could eventually create some pretty interesting opportunities. The latest Fed meeting minutes are out and I think what's happening right now is pretty interesting.
Almost every Fed official agreed that additional tightening was necessary, with a couple even suggesting that a rate hike larger than 25 basis points could be justified in December. Some officials were already pushing for a rate hike in October, and several remain concerned that inflation could stay elevated for longer than expected. But here's the weirdest part of all this. Oil prices have actually been coming down. Crude oil is now trading around $82 a barrel, down more than 21% over the past six months. You would normally expect falling energy prices to help ease inflationary pressures, yet the Fed is still discussing the possibility of even more aggressive rate hikes.
To me, this raises an interesting question. Is the Fed seeing inflationary pressures elsewhere in the economy that are much more persistent than investors realize, or are they risking overtightening into an economy that's already showing signs of weakness? Either way, I think the market is in a pretty difficult position right now, especially with all the uncertainty we're already dealing with.

NAND prices are expected to start falling in the second quarter of 2027 as China's YMTC aggressively expands capacity.
DRAM is a different story. TrendForce does not expect DRAM prices to turn lower through the end of 2027.

Jensen Huang might actually be making a comeback to NVIDIA and things are getting pretty interesting behind the scenes.
According to a new exclusive report from Semafor, some NVIDIA board members are continuing to push for Jensen Huang to return as CEO, despite the company publicly stating that it has no plans to bring him back. Apparently, there's a faction within the board that believes reinstating Jensen would be the right decision, which suggests the board might not be as united as NVIDIA wants investors to believe. Jensen himself has already said he would be honored to return if the board decided it was in NVIDIA's best interests. So the biggest obstacle right now isn't necessarily Jensen's willingness to come back, but rather whether the directors opposing his return can be convinced to change their minds.
Meanwhile, NVIDIA is reportedly considering other candidates, including Arm CEO Rene Haas and Marvell CEO Matt Murphy. However, Haas reportedly has concerns about taking the job while there's still a public campaign to bring Jensen back. And honestly, I can't blame him. Imagine becoming CEO of NVIDIA while half the industry is calling for your predecessor to return. Another interesting detail is that Jensen still owns roughly 3.5% of NVIDIA, which could potentially give him some influence over the board through shareholder voting mechanisms. That doesn't guarantee anything, but it means he's not entirely powerless in this situation.
Personally, I think bringing Jensen back would be a massive positive for NVIDIA, especially given everything that's happened over the past week. The company just delivered incredible earnings, but there are still questions surrounding its leadership, the ongoing investigations, and whether it can maintain the same execution without the person who helped build it into what it is today. I'm not saying Jensen is definitely coming back, especially with the investigations still hanging over everything, but I think the possibility is becoming harder to dismiss. And if more directors start supporting his return, things could change pretty quickly.
Melvin (@MelvinInvests)
If you own ANY AI stocks, you need to read this.
“Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us. And employees are committed.” That was how NVIDIA's interim CEO Colette Kress ended what might be one of the most important earnings calls in the company's history. NVIDIA came into this quarter facing some serious concerns. Jensen Huang's departure, circular financing, the sustainability of AI spending, declining margins, export restrictions, and whether the company could continue executing without its founder. And I think management did a pretty good job addressing most of them.
First, the numbers were absolutely incredible. NVIDIA reported $116 billion in quarterly revenue, more than doubling year over year and growing 20% sequentially. Data center revenue reached $108 billion, up 21% quarter over quarter, while Vera Rubin generated nearly $20 billion in its first quarter of production shipments, making it the fastest product ramp in NVIDIA's history. Management also guided for $130 billion in Q4 revenue and raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook from 70% to 75%. Think about that for a second. We're talking about a company already generating more than $100 billion in quarterly revenue that still expects 75% annual growth in fiscal 2028. One of the biggest concerns was obviously Jensen Huang's departure. Interestingly, Jensen was only mentioned twice by name during the entire call. It almost felt like management wanted to distance the conversation from Jensen and shift investors' attention back to the business. The board explicitly stated that Jensen would not return as CEO and refused to discuss the ongoing investigation. Instead, Colette emphasized that NVIDIA's employees, leadership team, customers, and suppliers remain fully committed. She even mentioned that TSMC's leadership had been in NVIDIA's offices this week. The company also confirmed that Vera Rubin Ultra remains on track for next year, with Feynman expected in 2028. Now, despite the board saying Jensen isn't coming back, I personally still think there's a small chance we could eventually see him return in some capacity. I wouldn't bet on it, but I wouldn't completely rule it out either.
Another major concern was circular financing, particularly NVIDIA's financial relationships with neoclouds and other AI infrastructure companies. Investors have been worried that NVIDIA is essentially financing customers who then purchase its GPUs. Management clarified that many of its guarantees only take effect once customers have secured financing and their infrastructure is ready for deployment. If those conditions aren't met, certain commitments can be reduced or eliminated. Colette also confirmed this wasn't a new policy, just additional disclosure explaining how the arrangements work. On market crashes like today, I'm reminded of a piece of advice I got from a CIO mentor that traded during the dotcom and 08 crashes and lived to tell the tale.
He said: "Treat investing the same way you treat life."
That's all. It has stuck with me for many years because after filling in the blanks, you're forced to become "better" in both portfolio management and life management. It's uncanny how correlated they are.
Strip either one down and you're left with the same raw materials: time and uncertainty.
Every investment gives up something certain today for something uncertain tomorrow. So does nearly everything that matters in life. Love, learning, raising a child, starting a new job. Anything.
Both reward patience, but only after testing it.
You can't generate performance without risking losses, the same way you can't love without risking grief.
But fundamentally, the first rule of portfolio and life management is survival.
You can come back from most losses, but not from the one that takes you out of the game.
It's always darkest before the dawn.

Now that we're close to 2027 it's a good idea to stress test downside scenarios where you have:
1. Capex cuts past 2028
2. Stranded Compute / DC Slowdowns
3. Finance deterioration (base case)
4. 2x+ rate hikes
Working in parallel and see what happens with valuations of AI longs.
If you see acceleration despite all 4, I'd argue that's an opportunity.
> Next-gen of photonics is one of the rare segments with an extreme rise in optical content and ASPs that can offset aggregate capex cuts.
Everyone’s moving into that space, including Elon Musk doing M&A, Marvell, Samsung and others with M&A… and we haven’t seen economic impact on emerging architectures even hit players from Celestial to Ayar + their suppliers yet.
If we look at a scenario where there's excess GPUs but power constraints:
We might see slowdown in aggregate accelerator/GPU/ASIC procurement, but your optical engines + light sources + switches players see acceleration.
Especially as incentive to replace power inefficient networking... since different (cheap BOM) optical architectures improves GPU utilization or even HBM requirements.
So value migrates to players more high-beta to architectural shifts.
If Celestial projections are $500m -> $1B, and we expect -30% aggregate capex cuts, I'd argue we'd still see upward revisions from Celestial over the next 2 years.
But financing with #3 matters a lot as seen with $AAOI dropping off of a $550M, vs. $COHR getting prepayments for capacity expansion from their customers.
Companies that rely on external foundries might be less sensitive to #3 since they're not as capex intensive.
On the other hand, companies in sectors have a lot of floating interest like certain Neoclouds, and require further financing might be the most impacted.
> Legacy and specialty memory is a different cycle that markets conflate with AI capex.
If consumer demand weakens but at the same time, players like Windbond exits DDR2, pricing durability is longer than markets expect.
> Wafer/substrate procurement such as ABF, SOI, InP are low cost but large downstream destruction if not secured, so we’ll likely see acceleration here as seen with $NVDA earnings call.
> qualification cycle players within bottlenecks remain very compelling, since first revenue in a large TAM, relative to MC is material to that company.
If a company is valued at $400m then they get a $200m of orders, it's more asymmetrical to a certain company than a rounding error to a $50B incumbent revenue.
_
There’s period of times where prices are dislocated from fundamentals from leveraged players getting wiped. I’d argue that time is now.
I disagree with a lot of the stupid "it's over takes" but I agree it's a good idea to haircut future capex expectations and forward valuations due to financing tightening + macro.
It's also good idea to see the nuances and stress test downside cases.
But TLDR: I'd argue next phase of AI infrastructure is going to be increasingly disconnected from aggregate AI capex growth.
I just personally wrote 4 things I'm using to stress test jointly some of the names I'm looking at, so I'm more comfortable waiting things out... despite seeing hedge funds getting liquidated left and right and overwhelming short positioning.
I personally see acceleration in more narrow parts of the supply chain, while markets treat the entire AI trade as one.
We'll see how things play out on longer horizons.

2027 年が近づいている今、次のような下振れシナリオをストレス テストすることをお勧めします。

2. コンピューティングの孤立 / DC の速度低下
3. 財務悪化（ベースケース）
4. 2倍以上の利上げ
並行して作業し、AI ロングの評価に何が起こるかを確認します。
4 つすべてにもかかわらず加速が見られる場合、それはチャンスだと私は主張します。
> 次世代フォトニクスは、光学コンテンツと ASP が極端に増加しており、総設備投資削減を相殺できる数少ないセグメントの 1 つです。
M&Aを行っているイーロン・マスク、M&Aを行っているマーベル、サムスンなどを含め、誰もがその分野に移行しつつあります...そして、新興アーキテクチャーへの経済的影響は、CelestialからAyarまでのプレーヤーとそのサプライヤーにさえ及んでいるのはまだ見ていません。

アクセラレータ/GPU/ASIC の調達全体では減速が見られるかもしれませんが、光学エンジン + 光源 + スイッチ プレーヤーは加速していると考えられます。
特に、さまざまな (安価な BOM) 光学アーキテクチャにより GPU 使用率が向上し、さらには HBM 要件も改善されるため、電力効率の悪いネットワーキングを置き換えるインセンティブとして役立ちます。
したがって、アーキテクチャの変更により、より高ベータのプレイヤーに価値が移行します。
Celestial の予測が 5 億ドル -> 10 億ドルで、設備投資総額が -30% 削減されると予想される場合、今後 2 年間で Celestial による上方修正が見られると私は主張します。

items.title:
Jensen’s first public statement since leaving $NVDA.
The support for Jensen is absolutely overwhelming.
Can’t think of anyone else who is better suited to lead Nvidia and America’s future in AI
Jensen Huang (@JensenHuang)
Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.
I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.
I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.
Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.
Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.
Jensen

私は 53 年前にアメリカに来ましたが、アメリカ国民になったことは、私の人生の中で最大の贈り物であり、最も誇りに思う瞬間の 1 つです。 NVIDIA は私の生涯の仕事です。同僚とともにそれを今日の会社に築き上げることができたのは特権であり、光栄なことです。 NVIDIA のような企業が設立できるのはアメリカ以外にありません。私は我が国を愛していますし、NVIDIA も愛しています。

$GOOGL Threat Intelligence Group: “The era of autonomous attacks has arrived”.
- Fully autonomous vulnerability exploitation is now happening
- Adversaries transitioned beyond manual prompting to deploying autonomous multi-agent offensive frameworks
- AI is collapsing the window between vulnerability disclosure and exploitation
- Google believes cybersecurity defense must become autonomous too
by combining Gemini and other frontier models for reasoning + smaller models for continuous scanning.
I’d actually argue beneficiaries of this arms race are AI compute and infra providers, regardless of the cybersecurity winners.
Since cybersecurity will become a source of persistent inference consumption.
$AMZN CEO Andy Jassy's also quoted estimates earlier that 20% of AI tokens could go toward cybersecurity.
Believe it or not, the rise of persistent cyberattacks from hostile state actors… is a structural driver for long term compute demand.

推論用の Gemini と他のフロンティア モデル + 連続スキャン用の小型モデルを組み合わせることによって。
私は実際、サイバーセキュリティの勝者に関係なく、この軍拡競争の受益者は AI コンピューティングとインフラプロバイダーだと主張したいと思います。

信じられないかもしれませんが、敵対的な国家主体による執拗なサイバー攻撃の増加は、長期的なコンピューティング需要の構造的な推進要因となっています。

SOME PERSONAL THOUGHTS AHEAD OF WEEKEND
I wanted to share a few thoughts heading into the weekend because at least for me this has been one of most mentally exhausting stretches I've experienced investing in growth stocks.
And honestly one of the things I've found most difficult has very little to do with market itself since it's how much mental real estate I apparently occupy in the minds of certain "gurus" on this platform whom I've never met, followed or even spoken to.
I started sharing my thoughts on X back in 2023 simply because I genuinely love investing and wanted somewhere to talk about market, share my research and connect with people who enjoyed it as much as I did and I never imagined that would turn into an account reaching 100 million impressions every month or that I'd eventually find myself appearing on national television every week.
I'm incredibly grateful because this platform accelerated my career at a relatively young age and opened doors that otherwise might have taken me many more years to reach but I'd be lying if I said spotlight wasn't intense since the larger my audience becomes and more visible I am the more I've realized that success also seems to attract resentment from people I've never interacted with or affected in any way possible.
Daniel has a phrase for this that I think captures it perfectly because "hating up" is absolutely real especially online where people seem more comfortable attacking someone who has become visible than examining why that person's success bothers them in the first place.
Like I've had people accuse me of taking an investment idea from them despite fact that I don't follow them and have never even seen their work while others take a disagreement over a particular thesis and turn it into a personal judgment about whether I know anything about investing.
What I find especially strange is that some of these individuals are in their 40s and 50s have been doing this for decades and still seem determined to tear down a 33 year old who is simply willing to publish his research, explain what he believes and put his own money behind those convictions (I've never asked anyone to agree with me or suggested that my way of investing is the only way to succeed).
And I think that last part is important because I do all of this under my real name and face, publicly disclose what I own through my subs service, share my position sizes and actual dollars I've invested and expose myself to scrutiny over every good decision and every mistake along the way.
There's absolutely nothing wrong with choosing to remain anonymous and I respect anyone who prefers to operate that way but theres just a different level of personal accountability when people know exactly who you are and watch you explain your thesis on camera and follow your positions in real time and wait for first opportunity to use a bad outcome against you... just remember being wrong privately costs you money but being wrong publicly can also cost you reputation, confidence and peace of mind which is something I don't think people fully appreciate until they've experienced it themselves.
None of this is to suggest that criticism should be off limits because disagreement is a huge part of investing but what I truly struggle to understand is why disagreement so often has to become personal... especially during periods like this when so many people are already dealing with painful drawdowns and questioning decisions they made with the best information available to them.
Markets eventually humble every single one of us regardless of how experienced we are or how much success we've had and anyone who stays in this long enough will eventually experience a thesis that breaks or a position they sized too aggressively or a drawdown that exposes a weakness in their process or a decision they wish they could take back so that's why I think showing people grace matters so much because you never know when you'll find yourself on the other side of that experience hoping others will extend you the same understanding.
And also just remember it cost absolutely nothing to root for people, respect the work they're putting in and recognize that someone can be wrong about an investment without deserving to be ridiculed for it and I genuinely wish more people on this platform understood that being publicly wrong doesn't erase courage it takes to stand behind your own convictions in the first place.
And to the people who've made rooting against me a hobby I genuinely hope you find the same energy for your own work that you've found for mine because if you're spending more time waiting for someone else to fail than building something of your own then maybe my portfolio isn't what needs your attention.
I'll be here next week, same name, same face, same conviction.

週末に向けての個人的な考え
少なくとも私にとって、これは成長株への投資で経験した中で最も精神的に疲れる作業の1つだったので、週末に向けていくつかの考えを共有したいと思いました。
そして正直に言うと、私が最も難しいと感じたことの1つは、市場自体とはほとんど関係がありません。それは、私が会ったことも、フォローしたことも、話したことさえない、このプラットフォーム上の特定の「達人」の心の中で私がどれだけの精神的領域を占めていると思われるかということだからです。
私が X についての考えを 2023 年に共有し始めたのは、単純に投資が心から好きで、市場について話したり、自分の研究を共有したり、同じように市場を楽しんでいる人々とつながる場所が欲しかったからです。それが毎月 1 億インプレッションに達するアカウントに成長したり、最終的には全国放送のテレビに毎週出演するようになるとは想像もしていませんでした。
このプラットフォームのおかげで、比較的若い年齢で私のキャリアが加速し、到達するまでにさらに何年もかかっていた可能性がある扉が開かれたので、非常に感謝しています。しかし、視聴者が増えて知名度が上がるほど、成功は、私がこれまで交流したことのない、あるいは何らかの影響を与えたことのない人たちからの怒りを引き寄せるようにも見えることに気づいたので、スポットライトが強くなかったと言ったら嘘になります。
ダニエルはこれについてのフレーズを持っていますが、これはそれを完璧に捉えていると思います。なぜなら、「憎しみ」は絶対に現実のもので、特にオンラインでは、人々は誰かを調べるよりも、目立つようになった人を攻撃する方が安心しているようです。

Source:
Bill Ackman (@BillAckman)
I believe the @nvidia board is not acting in the best interest of shareholders nor in a manner consistent with their fiduciary duties.
What we know is that the board fired Jensen or forced his resignation for violating company policy and/or in response to the accusation of an affair with a spy.
They did so without careful consideration of the impact on the company, its customers, its shareholders or other stakeholders.
They rushed to judgment without the benefit of careful due diligence or even with a basic understanding of the facts.
How do we know this?
We know this by how quickly Jensen was fired and how little was known at the time of his firing.
It takes time to convene a board meeting. There was time, maybe, for one Zoom.
And this is a decision that should have been made by a board sitting in person and carefully deliberating the facts once they are known.
And they should have slept on the decision and met again the day after to discuss the facts, the risks and the other implications of their decision.
The timing and lack of information did not allow for careful board deliberation.
While boards can fire a CEO for an inappropriate relationship with a subordinate, it should not be an automatic decision. That is why we have boards comprised of humans and not agents.
A board should consider whether or not such a relationship was consensual or whether it was an abuse of power dynamics. And a board has to consider what the impact of the firing is on all stakeholders.
If I were in this board, I would not have rushed to judgment based on articles in the media. I would have made sure the board had all of the facts so it could make a careful and informed decision.
Boards of Delaware companies have a duty of care which means they must make informed, prudent and good faith decisions. This clearly did not happen here.
What law firm is advising this board?
Or is the board even taken good legal advice?
It doesn’t look like it.
And now the board is compounding its failures by insisting that there is no possibility for Jensen’s return as CEO.
Why is it in the best interest of the company to foreclose the possibility of Jensen’s return and to do so before all of the facts are known? This is yet another breach of their duty of care.
Furthermore, the board has launched an investigation whose scope is unknown. Investigations can be extremely damaging to a company and should be carefully targeted to address whatever facts need to be known rather than be overly broad in scope.
In short, this looks like a series of major governance failures by directors that panicked due to headlines in the media. They likely felt compelled to do something because they were afraid of looking bad in the media, not because it was the right thing for them company.
They couldn’t stand the heat.
The board’s conduct here is shocking for a company of this scale and importance to our country and the world at large, particularly at this moment in history.

私は、@nvidia 取締役会が株主の利益を最優先に行動していないか、受託者責任に沿った行動をしていないと考えています。
私たちが知っていることは、取締役会が会社の方針に違反したため、および/またはスパイとの不倫の告発を受けてジェンセンを解雇するか辞任を強要したということです。
彼らは、会社、顧客、株主、その他の利害関係者への影響を慎重に考慮せずにそうしたことを行いました。

これをどうやって知ることができるのでしょうか?
これは、ジェンセンがどれほど早く解雇されたか、そして解雇当時はほとんど知られていなかったことからわかります。
取締役会の招集には時間がかかる。おそらく 1 回の Zoom の時間はあったでしょう。

SHELBY CULLOM DAVIS TURNED $50,000 INTO $900 MILLION
In 1947, with no MBA and no formal investment training, Davis quit his job to play the market full time. His stake: $50,000 from his wife Kathryn.
By his death in 1994 it was $900 million, per Morningstar. That works out to roughly +23% a year, compounded, for 47 years.
He focused on a rather unloved sector: insurance. Most insurers were selling well below book value.
Between 1947 and 1949 the Dow fell 24%, while his 7 insurance stocks more than quadrupled in value.
It was not a straight line. Between 1973 and 1975, his $50 million portfolio shrank to $20 million.
He hung onto many of his largest investments for his entire career.
items.title_ja:

MURIEL SIEBERT PAID $445,000 TO BECOME THE NYSE'S FIRST WOMAN MEMBER
The date was Dec. 28, 1967. The NYSE had 1,366 memberships, per The Bond Buyer.
She had asked a client which big firm would give her credit for the business she brought in. His answer: "Don't be ridiculous. Buy a seat, work for yourself."
She needed colleagues to sponsor her application. Nine out of 10 turned her down, per Case Western Reserve University.
She paid with cash and a bank loan backed by her stock portfolio, plus an initiation fee of $7,515.
For almost a decade, the exchange had just one other woman member, and only for a few months.
items.title_ja:
ミュリエル・シーベルト氏はニューヨーク証券取引所初の女性会員になるために44万5000ドルを支払った
日付は 1967 年 12 月 28 日でした。The Bond Buyer によると、NYSE の会員数は 1,366 人でした。
彼女はクライアントに、自分が持ち込んだビジネスをどの大企業が認めてくれるのか尋ねたところ、彼の答えは「ばかばかしいことは言わないでください。席を買って、自分で働いてください。」でした。
彼女は自分の申請を後援してくれる同僚を必要としていました。ケース・ウェスタン・リザーブ大学によると、10人中9人が彼女を断ったという。
彼女は現金と株式ポートフォリオを裏付けとした銀行ローン、さらに開始手数料 7,515 ドルで支払いました。
ほぼ10年間、この交換会には他に女性会員が1人しかいなかったし、それも数か月だけだった。

ANTHROPIC'S IPO COULD MAKE THOUSANDS OF ITS EMPLOYEES MILLIONAIRES
Option holders were sitting on $119 billion in paper gains as of Sept. 30, at an average exercise price of $2.91 a share, per Reuters, citing the company's filing.
Options granted through 2023 carried an average exercise price of just 52 cents. The IPO range is $70 to $78.
Two private-market firms have tried to size it:
• Sacra estimates about 2,800 current and former employees could hold at least $1 million in vested equity
• Hill estimates 598 non-founder employees will hold at least $100 million
It wasn't just engineers. A 2024 job posting for an administrative role that included managing calendars and expense reports paid $140,000 to $190,000, and said equity would be "a major component of the total compensation."
Anthropic grew to about 5,300 employees as of Sept. 30, from roughly 940 at the end of 2024. Non-founder employees can sell up to 10% of their holdings on the first day of trading.

CATHIE WOOD SAYS HEALTHCARE IS THE MOST PROFOUND USE OF AI
The ARK Invest CEO says AI could cut the cost of bringing a new drug to market from about $2.4 billion over 13 years to $600 million to $700 million over 8 years or less.
That would give drugmakers more of their 20-plus years of patent life to sell them.
@CathieDWood also sees AI catching cancer in stage one or earlier through blood tests, and curing disease by combining AI, gene sequencing and CRISPR gene editing.
"Traditional analysts have a really hard time with curing disease. They kind of think it's a bad business because they lose their chronic annuity... Well, that's ridiculous."
She says insurers are already reimbursing about $2.2 million for one-time gene therapies for sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia. If a company could cure a common condition like bad cholesterol and charge $160,000, she says "this will be the blockbuster of the century."

INVESTORS EARNED +8.7% A YEAR. THEIR FUNDS EARNED +9.9%
Over the 10 years ended Dec. 31, 2025, the average dollar invested in U.S. mutual funds and ETFs earned +8.7% a year, per Morningstar's Mind the Gap study.
The funds themselves returned +9.9% a year.
The 1.2 percentage point gap is not fund performance. Morningstar says it reflects the timing and size of investors' purchases and sales.
It adds up to about 12% of the funds' total return.
In U.S. stock funds the gap was much smaller: investors earned +12.8% a year vs. +13.3% for the funds.
Same funds, same decade. The difference was when the money went in and out.

ファンド自体のリターンは年間 +9.9% でした。
1.2パーセントポイントの差はファンドのパフォーマンスではありません。モーニングスターは、投資家の売買のタイミングと規模を反映しているとしている。
これはファンドの総収益の約 12% に相当します。

items.title:
ONE OF AI'S BIGGEST "DOOMERS" COULD SEE HIS ANTHROPIC STAKE TOP $15 BILLION
Skype co-founder Jaan Tallinn has spent years warning that artificial intelligence could end humanity. Now, he's expected to be one of the biggest financial winners from Anthropic's IPO.
Tallinn was a founding engineer of Skype, which Microsoft later acquired for $8.5 billion. He went on to co-found two organizations focused on threats to humanity: Cambridge's Centre for the Study of Existential Risk and the Future of Life Institute.
But he also invested in the companies developing the technology he feared.
Tallinn was an early investor and board member at DeepMind before Google acquired it in 2014. In 2021, before Anthropic had even launched a product, he led its $124 million Series A funding round at a valuation of roughly $461 million.
His goal wasn't simply to make money.
"My philosophy has been that I want to displace money that doesn't care," Tallinn told Semafor in 2023, explaining that he wanted safety-conscious investors to have influence over AI development.
But by 2023, Tallinn was already questioning that approach.
After Anthropic and other AI labs he funded declined to support a proposed six-month pause in advanced AI development, he declared that "Plan A failed."
He even warned that Anthropic, despite being more safety-conscious than other AI labs, was "dealing with dangerous stuff."
Estonian business newspaper Äripäev estimated in September that Tallinn's Anthropic stake alone was worth nearly €9.8 billion, or roughly $11.3 billion at the time.
Based on that estimate and Anthropic's last private funding price, the proposed $70 to $78 IPO range could put his holding at roughly $13.4 billion to $15 billion on paper. Pricing above $80 could push that figure past $15 billion.
Those are estimates, since Tallinn hasn't publicly disclosed his exact current stake.
Anthropic $ANT is expected to begin trading Thursday, potentially at a valuation exceeding $1.4 trillion.
According to CNBC, some of Anthropic's earliest AI-safety investors initially viewed their investments almost as charitable donations, with little expectation the company would ever become profitable or go public.
items.title_ja:
AI の最大の「破滅者」の 1 人は、人類の利益が 150 億ドルを超える可能性がある
スカイプの共同創設者ジャーン・タリン氏は、人工知能が人類を滅ぼす可能性があると長年警告してきた。現在、彼はAnthropicのIPOによる最大の金銭的勝者の1人になると期待されている。
タリン氏は、後にマイクロソフトが85億ドルで買収したSkypeの創設エンジニアだった。彼はさらに、人類への脅威に焦点を当てた 2 つの組織、ケンブリッジの実存的リスク研究センターとフューチャー オブ ライフ インスティテュートを共同設立しました。
しかし、彼は懸念していた技術を開発している企業にも投資した。
タリン氏は、2014年にGoogleがDeepMindを買収するまで、DeepMindの初期投資家であり取締役でもあった。2021年、Anthropicが製品を発売する前に、評価額約4億6,100万ドルで1億2,400万ドルのシリーズA資金調達ラウンドを主導した。
彼の目標は単にお金を稼ぐことではありませんでした。
タリン氏は2023年にセマフォーに対し、「私の哲学は、無関心なお金を置き換えたいというものだった」と語り、安全性を重視する投資家にAI開発に影響力を与えたいと説明した。
しかし、2023 年までに、タリンはすでにそのアプローチに疑問を抱いていました。
彼が資金提供したAnthropicやその他のAI研究所が高度なAI開発の6か月の一時停止案への支持を拒否したことを受け、同氏は「計画Aは失敗した」と宣言した。
彼は、Anthropic が他の AI 研究所よりも安全性を重視しているにもかかわらず、「危険なものを扱っている」とさえ警告しました。
エストニアの経済紙エリパエフは9月、タリンの人権株だけでも価値があると見積もった。

items.title:
The San Diego City Council voted unanimously to end the city’s license plate reader program, turning off about 500 Flock cameras.
The vote makes San Diego the largest US city to shut down its Flock network. Police say the cameras will go dark and their data will be deleted within 24 hours. In a separate 5-2 vote, the council also suspended the city’s “Smart Streetlights,” which record video used by police.
The program lost support after reports that a San Diego police officer may have used the cameras to track a domestic violence victim he allegedly had an inappropriate relationship with. A misidentification also left an innocent man jailed for a month. Three council members who backed the technology last year switched sides.

この投票により、サンディエゴはフロックネットワークを閉鎖する米国最大の都市となる。警察によると、カメラは暗転し、データは24時間以内に削除されるという。市議会は、5対2の別の投票で、警察が使用するビデオを録画する市の「スマート街路灯」も停止した。
サンディエゴの警察官が不適切な関係を持ったとされる家庭内暴力被害者を追跡するためにカメラを使用した可能性があるとの報道を受けて、同番組は支持を失った。また、誤認により無実の男性が1カ月の懲役刑に処せられた。昨年この技術を支持した市議会議員3人が寝返った。

Consumers are panic-buying at Costco, snapping up generators and other emergency supplies after a string of major tech outages, according to Mizuho Securities.
Mizuho analyst David Bellinger cited “increased emergency prep sales at Costco,” with 21 of Costco’s 26 high-priced generators sold out online as of Sunday night. He linked the buying to anxiety over the recent Microsoft Outlook outage, the nationwide FAA ground stop and “apocalyptic” concerns spreading on social media.
items.title_ja:

みずほのアナリスト、デビッド・ベリンジャー氏は「コストコでの緊急時備えの販売の増加」を挙げ、日曜夜の時点でコストコの高額発電機26台のうち21台がオンラインで売り切れとなった。同氏はこの買いを、最近のMicrosoft Outlookの機能停止、全国的なFAAの地上停止、そしてソーシャルメディア上で広がる「終末的な」懸念に対する不安と結び付けた。

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin warns that Iran-linked hackers have been targeting US critical infrastructure since the war began in February.
In written testimony to the House Homeland Security Committee on Wednesday, Mullin said Iranian government-linked hackers and pro-Iran cybercriminals have gone after transportation, healthcare, water, energy and financial systems. So far, he said, the attacks have caused only limited, localized disruptions, mostly against poorly secured industrial control systems, but weak security could allow far worse.
Officials say Iran isn’t behind the recent wave of US tech outages. “There is no indication whatsoever that there is any cyber malicious activity related to any of those incidents,” FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia told lawmakers. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said the outages were separate disruptions tied to maintenance and technical changes.
“We’re not under a systemic cyber attack,” said Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
items.title_ja:
マークウェイン・マリン国土安全保障長官は、2月に戦争が始まって以来、イラン関連のハッカーが米国の重要インフラを標的にしてきたと警告した。
マリン氏は水曜日、下院国土安全保障委員会での書面証言で、イラン政府関係のハッカーや親イランサイバー犯罪者が交通、医療、水道、エネルギー、金融システムを狙っていると述べた。同氏によると、これまでのところ、この攻撃は限られた局所的な混乱を引き起こしており、そのほとんどはセキュリティが不十分な産業用制御システムに対するものだが、セキュリティが脆弱な場合はさらに悪化する可能性があるという。
当局者らは、イランは最近の米国の技術停止の波に後れを取っていないと述べている。 FBIのクリストファー・ライア副長官は議員らに対し、「これらの事件に関連したサイバー悪意のある活動があったという兆候は全くない」と語った。国家情報長官のジェイ・クレイトン氏は、今回の停電はメンテナンスと技術変更に関連した個別の混乱であると述べた。
マルコ・ルビオ国務長官は「われわれは組織的なサイバー攻撃を受けていない」と述べた。

Nvidia $NVDA is moving up pay raises and stock grants to hold on to employees after Jensen Huang’s exit, per WIRED.
At her first all-hands meeting as interim CEO on Wednesday, Colette Kress told staff they’ll get raises and additional equity in December, months earlier than planned. Nvidia wants to “take care of each and every single employee that is here,” she said.
Pay was the top issue among about 700 questions employees submitted before the meeting. The next most common request was more transparency from the board, which the announcement didn’t address. Thousands of employees have reportedly lobbied for Huang’s return, but board chair Harvey Jones said Huang won’t be invited back.
items.title_ja:
『WIRED』によると、エヌビディア$NVDAはジェンセン・フアン氏の退職後も従業員を維持するために昇給と株式付与を前倒ししているという。
コレット・クレス氏は水曜日、暫定最高経営責任者（CEO）として初めての全員会議で、予定より数カ月早く、12月に昇給と追加資本を得る予定だとスタッフに伝えた。 Nvidia は「ここにいる従業員一人ひとりを大切にしたい」と彼女は言いました。
会議前に従業員が提出した約700の質問の中で、給与が最大の争点だった。次に多かった要望は、取締役会の透明性の向上でしたが、発表では取り上げられていませんでした。伝えられるところによると、数千人の従業員が黄氏の復帰を求めてロビー活動を行っているが、ハーベイ・ジョーンズ取締役会長は、黄氏は再び招待されないと述べた。

Muslims are projected to outnumber Christians as the world’s largest religious group by 2035, according to new Pew Research Center projections.
In 2020 there were about 2.27 billion Christians and 2.02 billion Muslims. By 2035, Pew projects about 2.57 billion Muslims and 2.52 billion Christians, and by 2070 more than 3.6 billion Muslims and just under 3 billion Christians.
The main driver is birth rates, not conversion. Muslim women averaged 3.1 children in 2020–2025, compared with 2.5 for Christian women. “It’s the babies,” said Pew demographer Conrad Hackett.
items.title_ja:
ピュー研究所の新たな予測によると、2035年までにイスラム教徒の数がキリスト教徒を上回り、世界最大の宗教集団になると予測されている。
2020年のキリスト教徒は約22億7000万人、イスラム教徒は20億2000万人だった。ピュー研究所は、2035年までにイスラム教徒が約25億7000万人、キリスト教徒が25億2000万人、2070年までにイスラム教徒が36億人以上、キリスト教徒が30億人弱になると予測している。
主な要因は転換ではなく出生率です。 2020年から2025年にかけてイスラム教徒の女性は平均3.1人の子供を産んだのに対し、キリスト教徒の女性は2.5人だった。 「それは赤ちゃんたちだ」とピューの人口統計学者コンラッド・ハケット氏は言う。

Israeli tanks have pushed into central Gaza in the first ground operation since the October 2025 ceasefire.
Forces crossed the “Yellow Line” separating Israeli- and Hamas-controlled areas, advancing along the main Salahudeen road into territory Israel had withdrawn from under the truce, residents say. The Israeli military says it is targeting “Hamas infrastructure.”
Dozens of displaced Palestinians fled their tents and shelters. Palestinian medics say at least one person was killed in an Israeli airstrike near the raid. Hamas called it a ceasefire violation and a “dangerous escalation.”
The operation comes as the US-backed Board of Peace overseeing the truce warns that both Israel and Hamas are failing to meet their commitments. Gaza health authorities say at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire began. Israel says five of its soldiers have been killed in that time.
items.title_ja:
イスラエルの戦車は、2025年10月の停戦以来初となる地上作戦でガザ中心部に突入した。
住民らによると、部隊はイスラエルとハマスの支配地域を隔てる「イエローライン」を越え、サラウディーン幹線道路に沿ってイスラエルが休戦協定から撤退した領土内に進軍した。イスラエル軍は「ハマスのインフラ」を標的にしていると述べた。
避難民数十人のパレスチナ人がテントや避難所から避難した。パレスチナの医師らは、襲撃現場付近でのイスラエル軍の空爆で少なくとも１人が死亡したと発表した。ハマスはこれを停戦違反であり「危険なエスカレーション」と呼んだ。
この作戦は、停戦協定を監督する米国の支援を受けた平和委員会が、イスラエルとハマスの双方が約束を履行できていないとして警告している中で行われた。ガザ保健当局は、停戦開始以来少なくとも1,600人のパレスチナ人が殺害されたと発表した。イスラエルは、この間に兵士５人が死亡したと発表した。

items.title:
Leopold Aschenbrenner is trying to relaunch his AI hedge fund as “Situational Awareness 2.0,” per the Financial Times.
The former OpenAI researcher has reportedly held talks with investors and prime brokers about raising fresh capital and returning to leveraged bets on AI stocks.
It’s a comeback attempt after a dramatic collapse. Situational Awareness returned 439% in the first half of the year, and its assets reportedly peaked near $45 billion. Then heavy leverage and sharp drops in AI stocks like SK Hynix, Sandisk and Nebius forced an emergency deal in July: the fund sold most of its public stock portfolio to Citadel and repaid its lenders, reportedly including Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan.
The fund still manages more than $10 billion, mostly in private investments. That includes a stake in Anthropic worth about $5 billion, which could rise sharply when Anthropic goes public this week.
items.title_ja:
フィナンシャル・タイムズ紙によると、レオポルド・アッシェンブレナー氏は自身のAIヘッジファンドを「状況認識2.0」として再スタートさせようとしているという。
元OpenAI研究者は、新たな資金を調達し、AI株へのレバレッジをかけた賭けに戻ることについて、投資家やプライムブローカーと会談したと伝えられている。
劇的な崩壊からの復活の試みだ。シチュエーショナル アウェアネスは今年上半期に 439% の利益を上げ、その資産はピーク時に 450 億ドル近くに達したと伝えられています。その後、高いレバレッジとSKハイニックス、サンディスク、ネビウスなどのAI株の急落により、7月に緊急取引を余儀なくされた。ファンドは公開株ポートフォリオのほとんどをシタデルに売却し、ゴールドマン・サックスやJPモルガンを含むと伝えられる貸し手に返済した。
同ファンドは現在でも100億ドル以上を運用しており、そのほとんどが民間投資となっている。これには約50億ドル相当のアンスロピック株が含まれており、アンスロピックが今週上場すると株価は急上昇する可能性がある。
